title: Welcome To The Jungle Drops Its Trailer Wednesday. Bollywood's Most Insane Ensemble Is Finally Here.
excerpt: Akshay Kumar, Suniel Shetty and Paresh Rawal reunite in a three-minute chaos reel alongside 30+ stars. The franchise's wildest entry yet hits theatres June 26.
body:
The three-minute trailer for Welcome To The Jungle will land on June 11 at a grand launch event in Mumbai — with every major name in this absurdly stacked cast showing up in person. If you grew up on the original Welcome (2007) and its unhinged sequel Welcome Back (2015), this is the reunion you've been manifesting since Nana Patekar first walked into Uday Shetty's house and decided to stay.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=dy_urGMFwH4

Akshay Kumar is reportedly in top form. The word from the industry is that his comic timing in this trailer is a throwback to the Hera Pheri era — the Akshay who could turn a line reading into a punchline without breaking a sweat. His chemistry with Suniel Shetty and Paresh Rawal is being called the trailer's single biggest highlight, and if you've ever watched these three share a screen, you already know why. Nobody does panicked masculinity funnier than this trio.

Directed by Ahmed Khan, the film keeps the franchise's signature formula intact: elaborate misunderstandings, a cast so large it needs its own zip code, and set pieces that make zero logical sense but somehow work because everyone is committing fully to the chaos. The jungle setting promises a new flavour of absurdity — think Welcome meets survival comedy, with designer clothes and enough one-liners to fill a WhatsApp forward chain for the rest of the year.

And about that cast. Buckle up.

Beyond the holy trinity of Akshay, Suniel, and Paresh, the film brings Arshad Warsi, Raveena Tandon, Lara Dutta, Jacqueline Fernandez, Disha Patani, Jackie Shroff, Rajpal Yadav, Johnny Lever, Shreyas Talpade, Tusshar Kapoor, Krushna Abhishek, Kiku Sharda, Daler Mehndi, Aftab Shivdasani, Urvashi Rautela, and a dozen more names who each carry enough screen presence to headline their own film. It's not an ensemble — it's a full-blown occupancy violation.

"The trailer of Welcome to the Jungle will be launched at a grand event on June 11 in the presence of the entire cast. It's around 3 minutes long and is loaded with laugh-out-loud moments, funny situations and one-liners." — Source close to production

For the diaspora, the Welcome franchise holds a special kind of nostalgia. It's the film your parents watched on a pirated DVD in 2007 and quoted at every family gathering for the next decade. "Ghunghat ke pat khol" became a ringtone. Nana Patekar's "Uday bhai" became a personality type. These films aren't cinema — they're communal property. The fact that this third instalment is arriving in a June already crammed with nine major releases, competing with everything from Cocktail 2 to Main Vaapas Aaunga to Bharat Bhhagya Vidhaata, suggests the makers are confident this trailer will punch through the noise.

The franchise's box office pedigree supports that confidence. The original Welcome earned over ₹100 crore on a ₹42 crore budget — a massive hit in 2007 terms. Welcome Back crossed ₹150 crore. With ₹1,400 crore reportedly at stake across all nine June releases, Welcome To The Jungle is positioned as the month's big closer, arriving on June 26 with the commercial swagger of a film that knows exactly what it is.

Raveena Tandon's return to the franchise adds another layer of nostalgia. She was one of 90s Bollywood's biggest stars, and seeing her share screen space again with Akshay — their Mohra and Khiladiyon Ka Khiladi pairing was peak 90s chemistry — is the kind of casting decision that makes a film feel like an event before a single scene is shot.

For NRIs in the US, UK, and Canada, Welcome To The Jungle will almost certainly get a wide theatrical release — the franchise has always performed well overseas, with the diaspora audience treating it as appointment viewing. The film's international marketing strategy is expected to leverage social media and targeted promotions to ensure that it resonates with Indian communities abroad. If you're the kind of person who books a whole row for your extended family on opening weekend, start the WhatsApp group now. This film not only promises to rekindle fond memories but also strengthens the cultural ties that bind Indian families across continents.

The trailer drops June 11. The film drops June 26. The chaos drops the moment Akshay, Suniel, and Paresh share their first frame together. Some things in Bollywood are simply inevitable.
